sentences.text: Listrognathosuchus was an extinct genus of alligatoroid crocodilian.
Charles Mook first described the species in 1930 after finding fossils in Torrejon Arroyo, New Mexico.
The generic name Listrognathosuchus was established in 1997 to replace Leidyosuchus for the species L. multidentatus.
Its parent group is Alligatoridae, and it is classified in the family Alligatoridae.
Listrognathosuchus is closely related to Borealosuchus.
Fossils of Listrognathosuchus date back to the middle Paleocene epoch, when the animal lived from 63.4 to 60.9 million years ago during the Danian to Selandian stages.
Researchers have debated whether it belonged to Diplocynodontinae, was a relative of later crocodylids, or formed its own subfamily called Leidysuchinae.
